title: Devin Alternatives: The Best AI Coding Agents in 2026
summary: Devin alternatives include free and paid plans at $20 monthly. Determine when to upgrade to Pro based on how many tickets you hand off weekly.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces


For the unattended work that last line ruled out, Activepieces runs flows on a trigger with nobody at the keyboard, across 747 integrations in an MIT-licensed open source monorepo.


It's a workflow automation tool, not a coding agent, so it connects an agent to your process rather than replacing one.


You build flows in it: a trigger fires, steps run in order, and results go to other tools. It writes no code on its own and won't replace what Devin does inside a repository.


If your complaint about Devin is the quality of its code, skip this entry and look at the coding agents above.


### When it fits the Devin task


It fits when your frustration is the work around the agent: someone copying a ticket into a prompt, someone checking whether the run finished, someone deciding whether the result ships.


To see the shape, use the flow below. A ticket card feeds a trigger.


The trigger starts a coding agent, and the output branches into a Slack message (the team chat tool where people hear about it) and an approval button, with Activepieces as the connecting layer.


Take from it that Activepieces owns the handoffs while the agent owns the code, so you can swap the agent later without rebuilding the process.


You also don't need a separate builder screen to set those handoffs up. Activepieces runs a per-project MCP server, so you can point Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf at that project's MCP server endpoint and ask for a new or changed handoff.


The tool calls it made, and the flow changes they produced, show up in the run trace.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production, and the MIT-licensed open source monorepo holds 747 integrations to wire those handoffs to, so most of your required integrations are probably already available.


For a small team, the approval button matters most. It keeps a human at the one point where a mistake costs you, and nobody has to watch the run to get there.


What follows from this is the cost question, because the platform is cheap and the agent behind it isn't.


### Cost and limit


Free and self-hosted is the bootstrap version: you run it on a small server you already pay for, and your only added cost is the time to maintain it.


If you'd rather not run infrastructure, the hosted cloud service is paid, so check the current plan page before you budget. Either way, the agent's own usage fees sit on top, and Activepieces won't reduce them.


The limit is plain: it moves work between tools and never judges the work itself. A bad agent behind a clean flow still produces bad pull requests, only faster.
